title: Integrated security & compliance playbook: RBAC, audit logging, data residency, SDLC, incident response, evidence workflows, risk & exceptions
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This integrated playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's policies and operational procedures for: RBAC & authentication, audit logging and log integrity, data residency & retention, secure SDLC controls, security incident response, compliance evidence workflows, and risk & exception handling. It is intended for engineering, security, and compliance owners responsible for controls mapped to SOC2/ISO and enterprise customer commitments.

Owners and scope
- Primary owner: Security (security-engineering)
- Secondary owners: Eng Infra, Eng SRE, Eng Platform, Product Security
- Scope: All Redwood-managed control plane components and hosted inference services (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, Private control plane components we ship).

1) RBAC and Authentication
Intro: We enforce least-privilege through SSO-backed group provisioning and role-based policies across cloud accounts, internal services, and the Redwood Console.
- Identity provider: Okta (SCIM for group sync and provisioning).
- Service identity: AWS IAM roles for services, short-lived STS credentials where possible.
- Human authentication: OIDC via Okta, mandatory MFA (TOTP or hardware key).
- Machine auth: JWTs for internal services (1h lifetime), mTLS for inter-service RPCs on the VPC/private networks.

Roles (examples):
- org-admin (very limited: billing, org config)
- security-admin (manage policies, access reviews, incident response)
- infra-engineer (deploy infra, manage IaC)
- runtime-operator (manage serving runtime, deployments)
- support-readonly (customer-support read-only views)

Enforcement and operational controls:
- All role grants must be via Okta groups; direct IAM user keys disallowed.
- Groups mapped to fine-grained IAM roles using Terraform-managed SAML/SCIM mapping.
- Periodic access review: quarterly for privileged groups, annual for non-privileged groups. Evidence: Okta group-member export (CSV) with reviewer sign-off.
- Emergency access procedure: time-boxed (max 24 hours), logged, and requires post-approval in the risk exceptions tracker.

2) Audit logging and log integrity
Goal: Centralize structured audit logs for authentication events, privileged actions, config changes, data-export requests, and security events. Maintain tamper-evident retention for compliance-bound artifacts.

Log format (application-level, JSON):
- timestamp_iso, request_id, user_id (or service_id), principal_type (human/service), action, endpoint, model_id, route, outcome (success/fail), latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, pii_masked (true/false), redaction_applied (true/false), region

Ingestion pipeline (standard):
- App -> structured JSON -> FluentD/Vector -> Kinesis Firehose -> S3 (encrypted SSE-KMS: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/redwood-audit-key) -> Splunk/Datadog (SIEM)
- Critical logs (auth, admin changes, SSO events) copied to a WORM S3 bucket with Object Lock (governance mode) for 7 years where contractually required.

Integrity and tamper-evidence:
- Every batch of log files is produced with a SHA256 manifest and HMAC signature stored in a separate integrity bucket.
- Periodic verification job (daily) validates SHA256/HMAC chain and raises alerts if mismatches occur.

SLOs and thresholds:
- Audit log ingestion latency (app -> SIEM searchable): < 2 minutes (P95).
- Alerting for pipeline failures: Pager duty to security-oncall within 5 minutes of failure.
- Log retention defaults: system logs 1 year, audit logs 7 years (enterprise). Customer data logs follow data residency/retention policy below.

Example CLI snippets:
- Enable SSE-KMS on S3 (example):
  aws s3api put-bucket-encryption --bucket redwood-audit-logs --server-side-encryption-configuration '{"Rules":[{"ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault":{"SSEAlgorithm":"aws:kms","KMSMasterKeyID":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/redwood-audit-key"}}]}'

- Example log entry (JSON):
  {"timestamp_iso": "2026-10-20T18:21:12Z", "request_id": "req-8a7f3d", "user_id": "user:alice@example.com", "principal_type": "human", "action": "model.rollout", "endpoint": "/v1/rollouts", "model_id": "rw-inference/fast-1", "outcome": "success", "latency_ms": 412, "tokens_in": "24", "tokens_out": "0", "pii_masked": "true", "redaction_applied": "false", "region": "us-west-2"}

3) Data residency and retention
Principles:
- Store customer data only within the region(s) contracted. Default hosted region: us-west-2 for NA customers, eu-west-1 for EU customers.
- Default retention windows are conservative; enterprise agreements may override.

Default retention policy (unless overridden by contract):
- Request payloads (raw inputs): 30 days
- Request metadata and traces: 365 days
- Embeddings and derived artifacts: 7 days (default); option to disable storage (0 days) at signup for privacy-sensitive customers
- Audit logs (security/administrative): 7 years (enterprise), 1 year (system)

Data deletion workflow:
1) Deletion request received (via support ticket or compliance portal)
2) Verify identity and scope, record request id
3) Trigger region-specific delete job: invalidate caches, delete from live DBs, remove from S3 paths, and add record to deletion audit log
4) Run background reindex/compaction to drop deleted artifacts from long-term storage (if applicable)
5) Report completion to requester, add evidence artifact to compliance bucket (S3 path).

4) Secure SDLC (software development lifecycle)
Requirements summary:
- Pre-merge gates: automated SAST (e.g., Semgrep), dependency scanning (e.g., Dependabot + OSS scan), secret scanning, and unit test coverage threshold (>= 80% for security-critical packages).
- PR process: 2 approvals required, at least one from the owning service team and one from security for privileged changes.
- Threat modeling: required for new public-facing services or services handling PII. Use the standard template in /eng-sre/how-tos/threat-model-template.
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions (or vault-integrated runners) with environment promotion (dev -> staging -> canary -> prod). Canary policy: 5% of traffic for 30 minutes with SLO monitoring before full rollout.
- Secrets management: HashiCorp Vault for runtime secrets; no plaintext secrets in repos.
- Pen tests and red team: annual third-party penetration test and quarterly internal purple-team exercises.

5) Incident response (security) procedures
Classification and initial actions:
- Severity matrix:
  - Sev-1 (Critical): Active data exfiltration or system-wide service compromise, production outage impacting customers
  - Sev-2 (High): Targeted credential compromise, lateral movement detected, partial service degradation
  - Sev-3 (Medium): Policy violations, suspicious activity without clear impact
  - Sev-4 (Low): Informational or confirmed non-impacting findings

Immediate playbook (first 60 minutes for Sev-1/Sev-2):
1) Triage: Security-oncall acknowledges within 5 minutes.
2) Appoint Incident Commander (IC).
3) Containment: isolate affected hosts, revoke service tokens/keys as necessary, rotate impacted credentials.
4) Preserve evidence: snapshot disks where possible, preserve network captures, export relevant audit logs to an isolated evidence bucket.
5) Customer communication: initial notification within 24 hours for incidents with confirmed customer data exposure; formal breach notification timelines (72 hours) follow legal/regulatory guidance.

Forensics and root cause:
- Forensics lead coordinates log collection (S3 paths), EBS snapshots, and copies of KMS access logs. Forensic artifacts stored in encrypted evidence bucket with restricted access.
- Post-incident postmortem: published within 10 business days for Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents, containing timeline, actions taken, root cause, and remediation plan with owners and ETA.

6) Compliance evidence workflows
Purpose: Streamline evidence collection for audits (SOC2, ISO27001, customer audits).
Workflow summary:
- Evidence matrix: a living spreadsheet mapping control_id -> required_artifact -> owner -> artifact_location -> last_updated -> comments. Security maintains the master matrix in the compliance repo.
- Automated evidence collectors: jobs that extract Okta access reports, S3 object lists for retention config, audit log integrity reports, IaC change history, and vulnerability scan outputs.
- Evidence cadence: quarterly refresh for controls marked as in-scope for SOC2; annual refresh for ISO/enterprise controls unless triggered by a change.

Evidence artifact examples and owners:
- RBAC enforcement: Okta group export CSV (owner: security-engineering)
- Audit log retention config: S3 bucket policy + KMS key policy (owner: eng-infra)
- Secure SDLC controls: CI job history, PR review evidence (owner: eng-dx/security)
contentcontinued:
- Incident response artifacts: incident timeline, forensics snapshots (owner: incident-response-team)
- Pen test report: third-party report (owner: security)

Evidence submission and reviewer process:
1) Owner uploads artifact to compliance S3 path and records entry in the evidence matrix with metadata (artifact_location, checksum, collector_job_id).
2) Security reviewer verifies artifact integrity and updates control status: compliant | non-compliant | exception.
3) Automated reminders issued 14 days before evidence expiration.

7) Risk & exceptions process
Principles: Exceptions are allowed only when compensating controls reduce risk to an acceptable level and the exception is time-boxed. All exceptions must have an assigned risk owner and expiration date.

Request process (steps):
1) Requester files an exception request in the risk tracker (fields: control_id, justification, compensating_controls, duration, requested_by, service_owner).
2) Security reviews and assigns a risk score (Low/Moderate/High/Critical) and recommends mitigations.
3) Exceptions > 90 days or rated High/Critical require CISO approval and exec sponsorship.
4) Approved exceptions are recorded in the exceptions register with an automated reminder at 75% of the duration to re-evaluate.

Example exception and compensating controls:
- Scenario: Temporary developer access to production database for emergency migration (requested duration: 48 hours)
- Compensating controls: session recording, break-glass audit, MFA re-auth, scoped read-only role where possible, post-action review within 3 business days

8) Ownership, SLAs, and metrics
- Security-oncall: 24/7 for Sev-1/Sev-2 events.
- Evidence refresh SLO: 95% of in-scope controls refreshed on schedule (quarterly/annual).
- Access review completion: 100% privileged groups reviewed quarterly with documented approvers.
- Audit log pipeline SLOs: ingestion P95 < 2 minutes; pipeline error rate < 0.1% monthly.

Appendix: Templates and runbooks
- Emergency access request template (fields): requester, service, justification, start_time, end_time, approver, post-action checklist.
- Evidence entry template (CSV columns): control_id, artifact_location, checksum, collector_job_id, owner, last_updated, comments.
- Incident initial triage checklist (commands):
  - Capture ephemeral metadata: curl https://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id
  - Export relevant logs: aws s3 cp s3://redwood-app-logs/2026/10/20/req-8a7f3d.log /tmp/evidence/
  - Snapshot EBS: aws ec2 create-snapshot --volume-id vol-xxxx --description "IncidentVolSnapshot"
